tb21_profile.skill: Write a numeric kernel (quadratic form x^T S x and dot product) in C behind a Python binding, keep it bit-close to a Python baseline (1e-10) and make it measurably faster at 5000-8000 assets
tb21_profile.domain: CPython C extension built with setup.py build_ext --inplace, float64 array math / linear algebra, benchmark harness
tb21_profile.task_form: fill-in-the-TODO implement-from-spec combined with optimise-to-a-measured-budget (>=1.2x) under an exact-numeric-equivalence constraint

searches: tools.py search all "times faster|speedup of at least|[0-9.]+x faster" -n 30
tools.py search rts "Python C extension|pybind|gcc -O|-O2|compile .*\.c |extension module" -n 20
tools.py search all "within .?1e-|tolerance of 1e|relative tolerance|numerically identical|match the baseline" -n 20
tools.py search rebench "allclose|Cholesky|covariance|matmul|numerical precision|float64 precision|numba|too slow|performance regression" -n 30

notes: TMax dominates honestly: it contains a whole family of port-Python-to-C-and-hit-an-Nx-speedup tasks, several of them with a skeleton plus a benchmark.py, which is TB2.1's shape almost exactly. Biggest false-positive trap here is the word 'portfolio': Recursive-Task-Synthesis has dozens of `pfm` investment-portfolio CLI chores with zero transfer, and I excluded all of them. TerminalWorld has essentially no C-extension performance tasks; its entries are benchmark-running rather than kernel-writing, so scores stay at 2-3. SWE-Smith is the weakest corpus for this task (pure Python bug fixes); I used dask array/linalg-vs-NumPy consistency bugs as the closest thing to a must-match-the-reference numeric constraint.
